## Contract review — PR #36961 (card #36915)

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `5f4ae21d5670dcc5a6e1e2b5f98b2c62c0e46213`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #36915 body and all five comments (triage 7127583168, claim 7127674243, round-1 dev report 7127788380, claim amendment 7127866157 ruling `Clause-②: yes` on route A, dev report 7130418813); the PR body; the 25-file net diff `origin/main...pr-36961`; the 58 check-runs on the head. Every check-run that ran concluded `success` (Test UI 16/16, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure). The rest were skipped by their path selectors or are opt-in. Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`@object-ui/types` `ActionResult.refusal?: { message: string }`** (`ui-action.ts:1364`): right. The member is optional and `ActionResult` is a closed interface, so no existing producer can already set a `refusal` of another shape: an object literal doing so was an excess-property error before this change. No implementer has to change, and a consumer that never reads the member sees nothing new. The four existing pins that `toEqual` the refused launch result were updated to expect the member. Their notice assertions are unchanged, so the pins are not weakened.
- **`@object-ui/types` `ActionContext.reportsRefusal?: boolean`** (`ui-action.ts:1237`): right as a type. It is optional and sits under the existing `[key: string]: any` index signature, so it is already assignable and nobody has to change. Putting the signal on the per-dispatch `ActionContext` instead of on the authored `ActionDef` keeps the authoring surface unchanged, which is the right side of the line. The jsdoc promises more than this PR delivers, though: see **S-1**.
- **One exit, both doors** (`flowLaunch.ts:308`, `withRefusal` at `:318`): right. `launchConsoleFlow` returns through `settled()` on the action door and on the trigger door. Its only other return, the action-door `!answered` case, is a dispatch refused before any fetch, which carries no judgement and so has no `refusal` follow-up to attach. `flowResponse.ts` stays read-only, as the claim requires (open PR #36845).
- **Row-menu path unchanged** (`useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:825`): right. The notice opens unless `context?.reportsRefusal === true`. The row menu dispatches through `ActionProvider.execute` with no `callContext`, so the flag is unset and the notice opens exactly as before. The PR's ablation A3 pins this both ways (the control stays green), and so do the new `refusedLaunch-9973` pins. Outside the runtime, the console's second flow-handler copy does not honour the flag: see **S-1**.
- **Grid hand-off** (`ObjectGrid.tsx:2883`, `:2896`): right. `runner.execute(action, { reportsRefusal: true })` goes through `scopedTo` (read, not reviewed), which shares every handler and merges the flag into the context for this one dispatch. The call context names no `objectName`, so `objectFields`/`objectActions` are not dropped. The provider's `loading`/`result` state no longer moves per row, and no `useAction()` consumer in `ui/packages` reads either value. The one routed `execute` override is bypassed too: see **N-2**.
- **Executor counts** (`useBulkExecutor.ts:523`, `:547`): right, and nothing is counted twice. `executeBulkBatch` (read, not reviewed) calls `perRow` once per id, and a refusal verdict exists only on a fulfilled `perRow`. So the refused ids of a batch are a subset of that batch's succeeded count, and `outcome.succeeded - batchRefused.length` cannot go negative. Refused ids are kept out of `outcome.errors`, and therefore out of `errors`, the error CSV (`downloadErrors` reads `result.errors` only) and the Retry buttons (rendered per `errors` entry). The filter runs over this batch's `validIds` alone, so an id is not counted again in a later batch. `succeeded + failed + refused.length === total` holds for a per-record run, and `BulkProgress.refused` keeps the processed counter and the progress bar adding up during the run.
- **Retry that comes back refused** (`useBulkExecutor.ts:665`, `:675`): right. The row leaves `errors`, `failed` goes down by one, and the row is added to `refused` (de-duplicated by id). The retry returns `false`, so `succeeded` is not touched. It reuses the existing `Math.max(0, failed - 1)` shape of the success path. The dialog disables the row's button while its retry is in flight, and the pin "retry() of a failed record that comes back refused" asserts `succeeded: 0, failed: 0, errors: []` and the single refused entry.
- **Dialog** (`BulkActionDialog.tsx`): right. Refused ids are removed from `succeededRows`, so the `landed.length === result.succeeded` cross-check still holds. The header icon turns amber when anything was refused. The refused list offers no Retry. `handleBulkDialogClose` keeps its `succeeded > 0` rule, so an all-refused run keeps the selection and does not refresh, which is correct for a run that wrote nothing. The empty-sentence edge case is **N-1**.
- **Internal type narrowing, not declared in the PR body**: `BulkExecutorOptions.runAction` goes from `Promise<unknown>` to `Promise<BulkRecordVerdict | void>`, and `BulkProgress` gains a required `refused`. Neither `useBulkExecutor`, `BulkExecutorOptions`, `BulkProgress`, `BulkResult` nor `BulkActionDialog` is exported from `@object-ui/plugin-grid`'s `src/index.tsx`, and the package's `exports` map has only `.` and `./style.css`. The narrowing is therefore internal, the PR body's "Nothing existing is narrowed" holds for the published surface, and no `(narrowing)` arm is owed.
- **i18n**: right. `grid.bulk.resultRefused` and `grid.bulk.refusedRecords` are present in all 11 locale files (ar, de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt-BR, ru, zh-Hans, zh-Hant). The PR body's "ten packs" plus the regenerated zh-Hant is the same 11. `resultRefused` is registered as count-neutral in `count-families-11445.test.ts`, beside `resultNotConfirmed`, and every pack writes it in the same "label · N" tally form as its siblings, so no plural family is owed. The plural-heavy locales hold up: ru `Отклонено {{count}}` is the neuter impersonal form (like `Не подтверждено`) and reads for every n, and ar `مرفوض {{count}}` follows `غير مؤكد {{count}}`/`فشل {{count}}`. The es/fr/pt-BR plural adjectives follow the precedent their own packs set with `Non confirmés`/`Não confirmados`.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset `.changeset/36915-bulk-flow-refused-count.md` lists `@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/plugin-grid`, `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n` at `patch`. Those are exactly the four packages the diff moves. `@object-ui/app-shell` is `private: true`, and the PR body says it is listed anyway, as sibling changesets do. `Check Changeset` is green.
- **`Clause-②: yes`** is right, and so is the line's form. The published `@object-ui/types` gains two optional members, which widens the public surface. That matches seat ruling 7127866157 and is the declaration face this review is owed for. No arm is written, which is allowed ("at most one arm"). `(narrowing)` would be wrong, because nothing published is narrowed.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`** is right. Both members are runtime types, and no metadata author can write either one. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening also ships `patch`, so `patch` is the right level for `@object-ui/types`. Both declaration lines are line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev open_questions**: the final report 7130418813 has none. The round-1 question (widen the surface: A/B/C) was answered by the seat's amendment 7127866157 (route A), and the diff follows route A.
- **Dev-declared narrowings**:
  - The local app-shell run was narrowed to 106 files. CI's `Test UI` (16/16 shards) ran the whole package and is green.
  - `check:query-options-erasure` and `check:type-check-debt` were not measured locally. CI's `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure` and `Type Check · debt ledger` are green on this head.
  - Build Core was skipped by its path selector, which is correct for a `ui/`-only diff.
  - All of these narrowings are answered.
- **Files against the amended claim**: 23 of the 25 paths are named by amendment 7127866157 (its files, their tests, the i18n packs and the parity pin, one changeset). The other two are `RecordDetailView.flowDoneSuccessMessage-12274.test.tsx` and `RecordDetailView.refusedLaunch-9973.test.tsx`. Each changes one `toEqual` to add `refusal: { message }`, which is the `flowLaunch.ts` output seen through the second host. They are tests of a claimed file and would go red without the change, so they are accepted. `flowResponse.ts` and `ActionRunner.ts` are untouched, as the claim requires.
- **Out of scope**: the paused-screen sibling is routed to mailbox #36743 (comment 7127841220) and is named in the PR body. Accepted.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5)**: no finding. The diff is client-side counting and rendering of per-record answers. The per-record fan-out (N action calls) is the existing contract the card names, and the diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- **Author**: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no separate author note is owed.

**Findings**

- **S-1 · should-fix**: the console's second flow handler does not honour `reportsRefusal`, but the published jsdoc promises that it does.
  - `ActionContext.reportsRefusal` (`ui-action.ts:1226-1237`) promises that with the flag set "a handler opens no refusal surface of its own". The console has two copies of the flow handler that share `launchConsoleFlow`. Only `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:825` gained the condition. `RecordDetailView.tsx:2329` still calls `setFlowRefusal` on every `refusal` follow-up, whatever the flag says.
  - `RecordDetailView`'s `ActionProvider` replaces the console runtime's provider for everything on a record page. A record page can embed a `list-view` component: `ComponentPropsMap['list-view']` spreads `ListViewSchema.shape`, which includes `bulkActions`. So a per-record bulk flow run from such a list reaches this handler.
  - There the count is right, because `settled()` sets `refusal` for both hosts. But the card's second symptom comes back: one last-write-wins `FlowRefusalNotice` is stacked on the result dialog.
  - Fix: either add the same `context?.reportsRefusal !== true` condition, with a pin, in `RecordDetailView`'s handler, which needs a claim amendment because that file is outside the amended surface; or file a follow-up card now and narrow the jsdoc to the hosts that honour the flag until it lands.
- **N-1 · nit**: a refusal with an empty sentence renders as a bare "Name:".
  - The refused list (`BulkActionDialog.tsx:698`) renders `Name: {message}`. When the producer sent no `refusalMessage`, which the types' jsdoc allows (`''`), the line reads as a record name followed by nothing. `FlowRefusalNotice` handles the same case by falling back to its title.
  - The spec already refuses `outcome: 'refused'` without a `message` at authoring time, so this is cosmetic.
- **N-2 · nit**: the grid's bulk dispatch now bypasses any `execute` override on the action context.
  - `runBulkActionRecord` now calls `useAction().runner` directly, so a routed `execute` on the action context is bypassed for bulk dispatches. The one such override in the repo is `RelatedList`'s `enlargedGridActions` (`RelatedList.tsx:3997-4011`). Today it is unreachable, because that grid's schema carries no `bulkActions`.
  - The PR body's read-first item 1 names the `loading`/`result` change but not this one. It is worth one sentence there or in the `runBulkActionRecord` comment, so that a later routed context knows bulk dispatches skip it.

**What holds.** `withRefusal` in `flowLaunch.ts` `settled()` sets `ActionResult.refusal` at the one exit that both launch doors return through. The grid's `runBulkActionRecord` dispatches through `runner.execute(…, { reportsRefusal: true })` and resolves a `BulkRecordVerdict` on a refusal. `useBulkExecutor` moves refused ids out of the batch's succeeded count, limited to the current batch (`perRow` runs once per id, and a refusal can only come back on a resolved call). So `succeeded + failed + refused.length === total`, refused rows stay out of `errors` (no CSV, no Retry), and a retried failed row that comes back refused moves to refused. The dialog draws "Succeeded 1 / 3 · Refused 2" with each row's own sentence. The console runtime's notice now skips only when `reportsRefusal === true`, so the row menu is unchanged; ablation A3 and the control pin show it. Both published `@object-ui/types` members are optional, so `Clause-②: yes` with no arm and `patch` are right. The changeset names the four packages the diff moves.

**S-1 (should-fix, from the contract review, confirmed).** The new published jsdoc on `ActionContext.reportsRefusal` says a handler that sees the flag opens no refusal surface. Only `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx` honours it. The record page's own flow handler (`RecordDetailView.tsx` ~2329, the `judged.followUp?.kind === 'refusal'` branch) still calls `setFlowRefusal` unconditionally, and its `ActionProvider` replaces the console's under a record page. A `list-view` embedded on a record page with `bulkActions` and a per-record flow action takes that path. The count is right there, because `settled()` serves both hosts, but the card's second symptom comes back: one notice, showing the last record's sentence, stacked on the result dialog. Preferred fix: give `RecordDetailView`'s branch the same `context?.reportsRefusal !== true` condition, plus a pin (a scoped dispatch with the flag opens no notice, and the control without it still does). That needs a claim amendment, since `RecordDetailView.tsx` is outside the amended surface; its two test files are already in the diff. The alternative is to narrow the jsdoc to the console runtime and file a follow-up card. The in-PR fix is a three-line change on the same seam, so I prefer it.

**Nits (no fix owed).**
- N-1. A refusal with an empty sentence shows as "Name:" with nothing after it in the dialog. `FlowRefusalNotice` falls back to its title in that case. The spec already refuses a refused end without a message.
- N-2. The bulk dispatch now calls `runner.execute` directly, so a custom `execute` on the action context, and its `loading` / `result` state, is skipped. The only custom one in the repo (`RelatedList`'s enlarged grid) has no `bulkActions`, so it is unreachable today. One sentence in the body would cover it.
- N-3 (L1). The running line shows ` · N failed` but no refused count. The progress bar does include refused, and the result line names it.

**Mechanical.** All-checks: 45 success · 13 expected skips · 0 failed · 0 pending. Floor checks are green, `mergeable_state` is clean, and `Fixes #36915` delivers the card once S-1 is in.

**REWORK** on S-1. The delta is a contract-review delta on the fix plus the L1 face on a green head.

  A second grep for flow handler registrations (`flow: …Handler`, `registerHandler('flow'`) finds the same two hosts, `useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:982` and `RecordDetailView.tsx:6353`, and no third. The dev's claim holds.
